findings.source_passage: the fear of the wild thing for the trap. It was a token that he was harking back through his own life to the lives of his forebears; for he was a civilized dog, an unduly civilized dog, and of his own experience knew no trap
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Nor did he open his eyes till roused'
findings.why_it_matters: The explanatory sentence establishing the atavism thesis — that Buck's instinctive trap-fear is evidence of ancestral memory because 'he was a civilized dog, an unduly civilized dog' — is the interpretive keystone of the chapter and the novel's central argument; the draft keeps the phrase 'fear of the wild thing for the trap' but drops the entire explanation, gutting the thematic meaning.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence: 'It was a token that he was harking back through his own life to the lives of his forebears; for he was a civilized dog, an unduly civilized dog, and of his own experience knew no trap and so could not of himself fear it.' This cannot be compressed away.

findings.source_passage: Civilized, he could have died for a moral consideration, say the defence of Judge Miller's riding-whip; but the completeness of his decivilization was now evidenced by his ability to flee from the defence of a moral consideration and so save his hide.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Not that Buck reasoned it out'
findings.why_it_matters: This is the novel's most explicit statement of Buck's 'decivilization,' named as such, and the Judge Miller's riding-whip callback is a critical interpretive link to Chapter 1; the entire sentence is absent in the draft, which jumps from 'He was fit, that was all' directly to stomach-driven theft, erasing the philosophical core of the passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full passage: 'All his days, no matter what the odds, he had never run from a fight. But the club of the man in the red sweater had beaten into him a more fundamental and primitive code. Civilized, he could have died for a moral consideration, say the defence of Judge Miller's riding-whip; but the completeness of his decivilization was now evidenced by his ability to flee from the defence of a moral consideration and so save his hide.'

findings.source_passage: It is true, it was a vicarious experience, else he would not have lived to profit by it.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'He had never seen dogs fight'
findings.why_it_matters: This dry, ironic narratorial aside is prosodically and rhetorically distinctive — it is one of London's signature intrusions of wry authorial voice and is widely noticed by critics as establishing the narrator's detached, almost sardonic stance toward Buck's education.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence verbatim immediately after 'his first experience taught him an unforgettable lesson.'

findings.source_passage: it was his ancestors, dead and dust, pointing nose at star and howling down through the centuries and through him.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'And not only did he learn by experience'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft drops 'pointing nose at star' from the ancestor clause, which is the structural echo ('he pointed his nose at a star... it was his ancestors... pointing nose at star') that gives the sentence its rhetorical power and makes the identification of Buck with his ancestors complete; losing the repetition flattens the cadence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full clause: 'it was his ancestors, dead and dust, pointing nose at star and howling down through the centuries and through him.'

findings.source_passage: No lazy, sun-kissed life was this, with nothing to do but loaf and be bored.
findings.why_it_matters: This phrase is the rhetorical contrast that gives the opening its punch — it ironically echoes the Southland idyll established in Chapter 1 and is stylistically distinctive in its rhythm.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore after 'flung into the heart of things primordial.'

summary: Two high-severity interpretive losses gut the chapter's atavism thesis: the 'unduly civilized dog' explanatory sentence and the entire 'completeness of his decivilization / Judge Miller's riding-whip' passage are absent, with additional medium losses in narratorial voice.
